liveness_probe.note: A first verification pass (script pb_mint_final2.py) had a bug: probe screenshots were rendered from a stale, unstepped env object (the fresh per-button env was used only for the RAM/OAM diff, not for save_frame). This was CAUGHT by re-inspecting the images -- 7 different button holds produced 7 pixel-identical PNGs, which is itself the tell -- and re-run correctly (pb_verify_clean.py) rendering each probe's own env. The numbers below are from the corrected run; screenshots are runs/onboard_wave5/power_blade_verify_*.png.
liveness_probe.probe: fresh NESEnvironment; load candidate state; hold each of RIGHT/LEFT/UP/DOWN/A/B/NOOP for 120 frames independently from the same reload; diff full 2KB RAM + peek_oam() against an unstepped base

long_hold_check.input: RIGHT held continuously for 1500 frames (~25s), checkpointed every 300 frames
long_hold_check.visual: power_blade_verify_right_hold_300/600/900/1200/1500f.png show the camera scrolling into a corridor with a statue and ladders, revealing new geometry not visible at frame 0
long_hold_check.time_counter: HUD TIME counter genuinely decrements under RIGHT hold: 0998 (t=0) -> 0996 (120f) -> 0975 (1500f) -- ruled out a frozen/paused screen

liveness_probe.visual_contrast: RIGHT scrolls into a corridor with a statue/ladders; LEFT scrolls into open sky with clouds -- a completely different, opposite-direction view; NOOP leaves the player standing still in the entry doorway while TIME still ticks down. Both the RAM/OAM divergence numbers AND the rendered frames agree.

discover_observables.lives_candidate_CORRECTED: discover_observables' top-ranked lives candidate ($0530, 5/5 run agreement) was REJECTED after cross-checking under the exact Pool harness progress_signal_gate.py and the real solver use (reset_all() -> load_worker_state() -> one step_all(NOOP)): it reads 0 at the start state, which underflows to 255 on first decrement -- the identical instrument trap documented for Ninja Gaiden's $001F in progress_signal_gate.py. Substituted the next-ranked candidate that is non-zero under the identical harness: $07CA (4/5 run agreement, reaches_empty=true, spends_its_stock=true, reads 1 at start under Pool.reset_all()+load_worker_state()+step_all(NOOP)).

odometer_gate.note: RIGHT and LEFT both show a real, symmetric, bidirectional horizontal scroll axis that caps hard at gx~86-88 almost immediately -- the same shape as configs/darkwing_duck.yaml's odometer gate (a real axis exists, so per that established rule this routes to the solver smoke as the actual arbiter, not an automatic wall verdict from the raw hold-only probe).

solver_smoke.finding: cells and max_gx were ALREADY saturated at the first 60s checkpoint (18 cells, max_gx=88) and did not move at all in the second 60s window -- explicit 'STALL WARNING: stuck at 18 cells for 2 min straight'. This matches, almost to the pixel, the raw single-direction odometer probe's independent cap (gx 86 under pure RIGHT, 87 under pure LEFT) -- THREE independent methods (naive RIGHT hold, naive LEFT hold, and a mixed 13-action/4-worker go_explore search) converge on the same ~86-88 gx ceiling with the agent still animating (OAM churning) throughout, not frozen.
solver_smoke.verdict: SIGNAL SOUND, EARLY WALL -- the state is genuinely live and controllable (see liveness_probe above); the search has not found a way past an obstacle within the first ~90 world-units of Sector 6 in the 2-minute smoke budget. This reads as a real early skill/route wall (an enemy, gap, or locked path just past spawn) rather than a broken start state or an instrument fault, but has not been root-caused further -- out of scope for this onboarding pass.
